item.title: Donald Trump challenges Alaska Senate trace
item.description:
The Department of Justice filed suit against the state of Alaska on Thursday, preemptively attempting to decertify the state’s election results—unless they win. Their justification: Democratic candidate Mary Peltola, who served as Alaska’s House representative from 2022 to 2025, is running against two men named Dan Sullivan, and that could be pretty confusing for voters. Dan S. Sullivan is the incumbent Republican senator; Dan J. Sullivan Jr. is a retired teacher and registered Republican running as an independent. “Daniel J. Sullivan decided to run for Senator in 2026 as a Republican with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him,” the suit alleges. “The sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan.” If Peltola wins, the DOJ argued, the state should not certify the election…

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France as protests take place across Europe – as it happened
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron said protests not organized by trade unions would be banned, as the Élysée braces for further unrest ahead of demonstrations planned for Saturday. French cities have been shaken in recent weeks by vandalism and looting sparked by cost-of-living demonstrations, amid a broader crisis besieging the country’s lame-duck centrist government that has spiked French bond yields. In the face of deficits and discontent, Europe’s “ centrists seem out of ideas ,” The Economist argued, while far-right and -left parties seize opportunity from chaos. “ Politics is not a spectator sport ,” the founder of a new Spanish political party wrote, calling for “a center that stops being the guardian of the status quo and runs towards the future at speed.” — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Trump says he may move White House press corps to new location
item.description:
The White House’s press secretary vacancy won’t necessarily keep the briefing room closed. President Donald Trump’s communications director, Steven Cheung, told Semafor that the next briefing would come “soon” — but if it happens before the midterms, a new press secretary likely won’t be behind the podium. Trump is in no rush to name a replacement after Katie Zacharia’s abrupt exit, and one person familiar with the situation said a new pick will “definitely not” be named before the election. Trump is his own best messenger, as his advisers see it, and he’s traveling aggressively in a bid to boost Republicans. Trump and “his team are focused on the midterm elections,” Cheung added. The haziness surrounding press strategy comes as the White House continues to spar with the media, threatening legal action against Politico over its reporting on chief of staff Susie Wiles. item.description:

The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua news agency. item.title: Bodycam video shows police shooting death of one-year-old Kohen Wiley – deconstructed
item.description:

item.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries
item.description:
When the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act was still a work in progress, the Senate briefly inserted a ban on corporate ownership of single-family rental housing so sweeping that it might well have killed off the small but growing build-to-rent sector. After furious activism by the housing supply boosters, who had been the main advocates for the law's many other provisions, that investor ban was significantly pared back. The final version of ROAD, which became law in July , prohibits investors who own 350 single-family rental homes from buying new ones. But it also includes a long list of exemptions for large investor purchases of single-family rentals. The primary exemptions include homes purchased as part of a build-to-rent project and dilapidated homes that the investor spends significant money renovating. item.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes
item.description:
PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said. The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry. Continue reading...
